title: Multi-object selection: marquee selects all overlapping objects, shift-click adds/removes, group ops apply to all
description:
## Problem

The selection tool currently supports selecting only one object at a time. A deliberate comment in Shell.tsx (line 3116) says: "multi-select is not yet supported; select any for now". The marquee drag in StageArea.tsx (lines 2242–2256) also only picks the first overlapping object (`.find()`), not all of them. `handleSelectAll` (Edit > Select All) similarly only selects the last object in the keyframe.

Multi-selection is essential authoring UX: it gates align/distribute workflows, enables moving multiple objects together, and is required for meaningful group creation (currently group always wraps a single object).

## What to implement

### 1. Selection state

- Change `selectedShapeId: string | null` in Shell.tsx to `selectedShapeIds: string[]` (or a `Set<string>`).
- Update all downstream consumers: TransformPanel, PropertiesPanel, FiltersPanel, AlignPanel, copy/cut/paste/delete handlers. Single-object-only panels (PropertiesPanel, FiltersPanel, SoundPanel) show their content only when exactly one object is selected.

### 2. Marquee selects all overlapping objects

- In StageArea.tsx `handleMouseUp`, when the selection tool finalises a marquee, collect **all** objects whose bounds overlap the marquee rect (not just `.find()`), and call `onShapeSelect` with the full array.

### 3. Shift+click adds/removes from selection

- In StageArea.tsx click handling (arrow/selection tool), check `e.shiftKey`. If the clicked object is already selected, remove it; otherwise add it to the existing set.

### 4. Select All

- `handleSelectAll` in Shell.tsx should collect all display objects from the governing keyframe of the active layer and select them all.

### 5. Move/delete multi-selection

- When multiple objects are selected and the user drags one, move all selected objects by the same delta.
- Delete (Backspace/Delete key) removes all selected objects.

### 6. AlignPanel

- AlignPanel already receives a list of objects; wire it to the real multi-selection set.

## Acceptance criteria

- Rubber-band drag selects all objects inside the marquee; each shows selection handles.
- Shift+clicking additional objects adds them to the selection.
- Edit > Select All selects all objects on the active keyframe.
- Moving any selected object moves all selected objects together.
- Delete removes all selected objects.
- Align/Distribute operations (AlignPanel) apply to the multi-selection.
- Single-selection panels (Properties, Filters, Sound) remain visible only when exactly one object is selected; with >1 selected they show a "Multiple objects selected" placeholder.
